data.body: B190 appends a per-clone suffix to derived agent ids ({host}-{tree} -> {host}-{tree}-{hex6}). A lease claimed before the upgrade under the bare derived id stays live, but after the upgrade every holder comparison (leases.renew/_transition, api/gates.py:221, api/jobs.py:51, core/schedule.py:412/421) sees it as someone else's: heartbeat says 'no lease held', complete/merge refuse, claim refuses. The commit hook is fine (enforce.py same_tree rule). Workaround today: release/re-claim with --agent <old id> (as_agent over MCP). Fix: treat the bare derived id of THIS clone as an alias of the suffixed one for leases whose holder equals it, only when this clone has no shard/lease under the suffixed id for that item — and say so in `ddflow identify`. Regression test: claim under the bare id, create .ddflow/local/clone-id, heartbeat must succeed.
data.title: Upgrade path for B190: a lease held under the pre-suffix derived id is not "mine" after upgrade

data.body: Seen on B190 (2026-09-28): the critic review took 2055 s over 6 chunks; the Claude Code MCP client aborted at 1800 s with no progress notification. The gate was recorded (partial, 2 findings) but the evidence holds only finding TITLES, so the findings themselves existed only in the lost tool response — the review had to be re-run from the CLI (another ~35 min). Fix: (1) store each finding's body/claim/probe in the gate evidence or an output_file under .ddflow/local/reviews/ whose digest is recorded; (2) emit MCP progress notifications per chunk so the client's idle timer resets. Regression test: a fake reviewer returning a finding; the recorded evidence carries its body.
data.title: ddflow_review outlives the MCP idle timeout and its finding bodies are lost: persist them in the gate evidence and send progress

data.rule: Several agents file B-numbers concurrently and task add overwrites an existing id without error, so 'the next free number' guessed from one agent's view clobbers another agent's item (even a running one). Before task add, confirm the id is unused (`ddflow show <id>` must fail), and prefer a descriptive id (B-json-failures) that no other agent will pick.
data.title: With parallel agents, never file a task under the 'next' sequential id: check it is free, or use a descriptive id

data.how: For a fix of a conservative (safe-direction) bug, write the invariant the old behaviour guaranteed as a property test first (nothing overlapping vanishes; no live tree is advised for removal), then fix the misleading part without weakening it.
data.rule: A remedy string that names a command which does not exist is inert: whoever follows it gets an error. Correcting it to a real command (git worktree remove, ddflow cleanup --apply, a delete) activates every place it was ever printed, including cases the old text was wrong for. Before turning advice into a working destructive command, enumerate the states that reach it (adopted/harness-owned trees, live leases, unmerged work) and test the ones that must not get it.
data.title: Making advice runnable makes it dangerous: when a remedy stops naming a nonexistent command, re-check every condition under which it is printed
data.why: 2026-09-29 B-fix-remedy-texts: fixing 'ddflow worktree remove' to 'git worktree remove <path>' made recover advise deleting a harness session's own adopted worktree; the old nonexistent command had been harmless. Same review round: B-fix-contest-overjoin's fix for an over-report dropped a real double claim. Both fixes moved toward the dangerous direction while fixing a safe-direction bug.
